overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by omitting candidates' names from the April 13 and April 27, 2026 notices and by failing to announce the April 13 meeting recording; ordered future compliance.

allegations.summary: First complaint: the April 13, 2026 notice's appointment topic did not list the name of the clerk candidate the Board later appointed.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law when it did not list in the notices the names of the candidates it planned to consider for appointment during the April 13 and April 27, 2026, meetings.

allegations.summary: First complaint: the Chair did not verbally announce at the April 13, 2026 meeting that the meeting was being recorded.
allegations.key_passage: the Board acknowledges, and we find, that the Chair failed to make the required announcement and thus violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Second complaint: the April 27, 2026 notice's firefighter appointment topic did not list the names of the call firefighter candidates appointed.
allegations.key_passage: Here, the Board did not assert that it did not know the names of the candidates to be considered for appointment during the April 13 and April 27, 2026, meetings.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
